# BeautifulRust clippy configuration. Copy to your crate or workspace root, next to
# Cargo.toml, alongside the [lints] block from lints.toml.
# Flag any function with a bool parameter, not just functions with four or more.
# A bool argument is unreadable at the call site (report(true)) and can't grow a
# third mode; use a two-variant enum or two methods instead.
# Allow unwrap, expect, and printing in tests, where a panic is the assertion.
# Paste this into your Cargo.toml (or replace [lints] with [workspace.lints] in a
# workspace root and add `[lints] workspace = true` to each member). It makes clippy
# enforce the rules from ../steering.md (BeautifulRust rust-best-practices) that a machine can check.
# Everything is "warn"; make CI strict with:
#     cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   (plus the feature set CI uses)
# Silence a lint locally with a reason, which the config below requires:
#     #[expect(clippy::unwrap_used, reason = "the regex is a literal and always compiles")]
# Lints marked [lib] fit libraries; applications can drop them.
# Groups first, at lower priority so the individual settings below win.
# Panics: return errors, and give every intentional panic a reason.
# Suppressions must explain themselves and expire when no longer needed.
# Pedantic lints that are mostly noise in practice, or that the skill disagrees with.

# deepsec-gate.sh — the build-with-quality security gate, backed by deepsec
# Policy comes from the manifest ([security.deepsec] in $AGENTBOX_CONFIG,
# default /etc/agentbox.toml), overridable per key with DEEPSEC_GATE_<KEY>
# (e.g. DEEPSEC_GATE_FAIL_ON=CRITICAL). The gate never stores a credential:
# only the NAME of the env var that holds one is ever written to disk.
#   --diff <ref>        PR mode: investigate files changed vs <ref> (net-new findings gate)
#   --full              whole-repo scan + AI process (expensive; bounded by max_duration)
#   --scan-only         regex candidate scan only — free, never blocks
#          --dry-run (print the resolved plan as JSON and exit 0)
# Exit codes: 0 pass · 1 blocking findings (severity >= fail_on) · 70 deepsec
# runtime error · 78 gate unavailable or misconfigured · 124 max_duration hit.
# File-list paths belong to the invoking shell, not the internal workspace.
# Validate before availability probes so an input error never starts a model.
# ── Policy: manifest [security.deepsec] → env overrides → CLI overrides ──────
# ── Model route (persisted as non-secret config; names only) ─────────────────
# Evidence must be created by this invocation. Never reuse a previous comment,
# export or receipt when interpreting deepsec's overloaded exit code 1.
# NOTE: deepsec 2.3.9 (the pinned/baked CLI) accepts only --project-id,
# --root and --matchers on `scan`, and rejects unknown options with exit 1.
# It renders no TUI when stdout is not a TTY, which is how the gate runs it.
# deepsec 2.3.10 also exits 1 for invalid inputs, quota exhaustion and agent
# failures. In direct mode it writes --comment-out only AFTER successful batch
# completion, when new findings exist. A fresh nonempty comment disambiguates 1.
# PR mode: 0 = completed/no findings, 1 + fresh comment = findings.
# scan-only / full: any non-zero is a runtime error.
